blocks.text: 低延迟推理为针对特定模型、硬件和工作负载的优化提供了许多机会。这些优化通常需要大量的内核融合以及跨实现复制代码，使其难以维护。为支持这种特化，我们推出SGLang 低延迟模式。它通过插件框架将专用内核引入 SGLang，并在 NVIDIA 和 AMD GPU 上大幅降低延迟。在四块 NVIDIA GB300 GPU 上的 AgentX 轨迹回放中，单并发会话下 P90 每用户 token 生成速度从671.2 提升至 928.4 tokens/s（1.38×）。在四块 AMD MI355X GPU 上，四并发会话下从331.6 提升至 516.0 tokens/s（1.56×）。每项结果均为同一硬件上低延迟模式与 SGLang 基线的对比。

blocks.text: 在单请求下，DSpark 每步验证六行 token，每个内核的工作量很少，而依赖关系和跨 GPU 通信会增加延迟。在预热后的 CUDA-graph 性能分析中，该插件将验证图从 1,205 个内核减少到 1,189 个，但将解码器层延迟中位数从 96.8 µs 降至 68.4 µs。收益主要来自减少等待和重叠工作，其中注意力区域的降幅最大。下表列出了这些变化，随后我们将逐一介绍主要优化。

blocks.text: 低延迟专用优化

inlines.text: 低延迟专用优化

blocks.text: 1. 在其输入存在之前启动下一个内核。 程序化依赖启动（PDL）允许内核在前驱内核仍在运行时启动。它可以在等待所需输入之前准备屏障、设置张量内存并加载权重。SGLang 已使用 PDL。该插件将依赖释放提前，使更多此类准备工作与正在进行的计算重叠。例如，MoE 归约在开始轮询对等结果时，就释放下一层的第一个投影。

blocks.text: 注意力路径还使用了针对小批量专门优化的投影 GEMM，并在加载 query 时应用 RoPE，从而省去一个单独的内核。在依赖关系允许的情况下，注意力会在等待 query 之前就开始收集 KV 数据。在单个请求下，该插件还会在步骤开始时将独立的 Engram 查找和投影移到侧流上。它们的 all-reduce 仍留在主流上，以保持跨 GPU 的通信顺序。

blocks.text: 2. 从 GEMM epilogue 发布投影输出。 在注意力输出投影之后，每个 GPU 持有一个部分结果，该结果必须跨 GPU 进行归约。SGLang 的标准路径使用两个内核：GEMM 写出其输出，然后一个融合内核将其读回，发送给对等节点，并执行归约、mHC 更新和归一化。

blocks.text: 该插件保留两个内核，但将发送移入 GEMM 的 epilogue。每个 CTA 在其他 tile 仍在计算时，直接通过 NVLink 多播存储将已完成的 tile 从寄存器发布到对等 GPU。消费者通过 PDL 启动，并在归约之前等待已发布的结果。这更早地启动通信，并避免仅为发送而重新读取部分输出。消费者的计算保持不变。

blocks.text: 3. 在路由完成之前启动专家 GEMM。 在低并发下，路由可能占据 MoE 路径的相当大一部分。在最多八行的情况下，每个专家选中的 token 可容纳在一个八行 tile 中。该插件使用位图和种群计数来放置这些 tile，无需扫描或排序，同时保留 SGLang 的 top-k 选择。它提前启动第一个专家 GEMM，使设置与路由重叠，并跳过填充权重中的全零 tile。标准内核已经使用八行 tile；收益来自更简单的路由、更早的执行和更少的浪费工作。在性能分析运行中，MoE 窗口中位数从 44.4 µs 降至 36.5 µs，而第二个 GEMM 或归约几乎没有变化。

blocks.text: 在低并发下，每个解码器层会运行数十个小内核和两次张量并行 all-reduce。三项成本占主导：

inlines.text: 在低并发下，每个解码器层会运行数十个小内核和两次张量并行 all-reduce。三项成本占主导：
启动开销：
HIP graph 消除了 CPU 的启动工作，但每个小内核在 GPU 上仍需 2-4 µs。
空闲边界：
每个内核必须完成后下一个才能开始，因此当一个内核排空、下一个内核启动时，计算单元处于空闲状态，权重加载也会暂停。
通信停顿：
每一层都要等待两次跨 GPU 的 all-reduce，期间没有计算在运行。

blocks.text: 每层两次持久化启动

inlines.text: 每层两次持久化启动

blocks.text: 持久化 FlyDSL 内核将每层的大部分工作合并为两次启动。K1 处理 mHC 更新、query 和 KV 投影以及 KV-cache 写入。K2 处理 attention、输出投影、剩余的 mHC 更新、MoE 以及两次 all-reduce。索引层在两者之间加入压缩、K2i 打分和 top-k。启动边界使 K1 的 KV 写入在 K2 读取之前对整个 GPU 可见。

blocks.text: 启动内部各阶段的重叠

inlines.text: 启动内部各阶段的重叠

blocks.text: 每个阶段产生的值都会与当前解码步的标签一起存储，因此下一个阶段（无论在同一 GPU 还是另一 GPU 上）只要标签匹配就会立即开始处理该值。步与步之间无需单独的标志或重置。不依赖路由的权重会在其输入到达之前加载：K1 的投影权重在 norm 完成前加载，K2 中 mHC 混合权重和共享专家的权重在它们要相乘的数据之前加载。路由专家权重在路由器选定专家后加载。

blocks.text: 该集成将启动准备与执行分离：

inlines.text: 该集成将启动准备与执行分离：
注册：
插件为其支持的每种模型架构注册一个规范。该规范描述实现的需求，并提供构建它的入口点。这为 SGLang 提供了一种发现外部实现的方式，同时将模型支持的细节保留在拥有内核的库中。
守卫：
专用内核会对硬件、精度、并行性和服务特性做出假设。SGLang 在加载权重之前检查声明的需求，以便不兼容的配置尽早失败。在构建插件之前，对已加载模型运行额外检查。这些检查区分不支持的服务器配置与受支持的服务器遇到插件覆盖范围之外的步骤。
构建：
权重准备和执行资源在初始化期间设置，以便请求可以复用它们。该集成适应每种实现的需求：AMD 可以在权重转换之前保留检查点张量，而 NVIDIA 接收一个绑定，通过它可以在运行时状态可用时访问该状态。SGLang 在确定 KV 缓存大小之前构建插件，以便其分配被计入，然后在模型的前向路径中安装调度。
运行时：
专用执行和通用执行共存，因为插件可能只覆盖某些步骤类型和 token 数量。安装的调度器使用插件的支持条件来选择其前向或 SGLang 的原始前向。张量并行 rank 必须在覆盖范围上达成一致，以避免进入不兼容的集合通信。此选择适合 ModelRunner 的现有执行流程。在图捕获期间，为相应形状记录所选路径；服务随后可以重放该图，而无需重复 Python 调度。

blocks.text: 这种设计让内核团队能够交付专注的优化，而无需将每个专用实现添加到 SGLang 的核心代码库中。它将集成工作集中在显式接口上，并允许每个库逐步扩展其覆盖范围。专用内核可以服务它们优化的场景，而 SGLang 的通用前向处理受支持配置内的剩余步骤。

blocks.text: Low-latency inference offers many opportunities for optimizations tailored to specific models, hardware and workloads. These optimizations often require extensive kernel fusion and duplicate code across implementations, making them difficult to maintain. To support this specialization, we introduce SGLang Low-Latency Mode. It brings specialized kernels into SGLang through a plugin framework and delivers substantial latency reductions on both NVIDIA and AMD GPUs. In AgentX trace replay on four NVIDIA GB300 GPUs, P90 per-user token generation speed increases from 671.2 to 928.4 tokens/s (1.38×) at one concurrent session. On four AMD MI355X GPUs, it increases from 331.6 to 516.0 tokens/s (1.56×) at four concurrent sessions. Each result compares low-latency mode with the SGLang baseline on the same hardware.

blocks.text: At one request, DSpark verifies six token rows per step, leaving little work for each kernel while dependencies and cross-GPU communication add latency. In warmed CUDA-graph profiles, the plugin reduces the verify graph from 1,205 kernels to 1,189 but cuts the median decoder-layer latency from 96.8 µs to 68.4 µs. The gains come largely from reducing waits and overlapping work, with the largest reduction in the attention region. blocks.text: Low-Latency-Specific Optimizations

inlines.text: Low-Latency-Specific Optimizations

blocks.text: 1. Launch the next kernel before its input exists. Programmatic dependent launch (PDL) lets a kernel start while its predecessor is still running. It can prepare barriers, set up tensor memory and load weights before waiting for the input it needs. SGLang already uses PDL. The plugin moves dependency releases earlier so more of this preparation overlaps with ongoing computation. For example, the MoE reduction releases the next layer’s first projection as soon as it starts polling for peer results.

inlines.text: 1. Launch the next kernel before its input exists.

Programmatic dependent launch (PDL) lets a kernel start while its predecessor is still running. It can prepare barriers, set up tensor memory and load weights before waiting for the input it needs. SGLang already uses PDL. The plugin moves dependency releases earlier so more of this preparation overlaps with ongoing computation. For example, the MoE reduction releases the next layer’s first projection as soon as it starts polling for peer results.

blocks.text: The attention path also uses projection GEMMs specialized for small batches and applies RoPE while loading the query to remove a separate kernel. Where dependencies allow it, attention begins gathering KV data before waiting for the query. At one request, the plugin also moves independent Engram lookups and projections onto a side stream at the start of the step. Their all-reduces stay on the main stream to preserve communication order across GPUs.

blocks.text: 2. Publish the projection output from the GEMM epilogue. After the attention output projection, each GPU holds a partial result that must be reduced across GPUs. SGLang’s standard path uses two kernels: the GEMM writes its output, then a fused kernel reads it back, sends it to peers and performs the reduction, mHC update and normalization.

inlines.text: 2. Publish the projection output from the GEMM epilogue.

After the attention output projection, each GPU holds a partial result that must be reduced across GPUs. SGLang’s standard path uses two kernels: the GEMM writes its output, then a fused kernel reads it back, sends it to peers and performs the reduction, mHC update and normalization.

blocks.text: The plugin keeps two kernels but moves the send into the GEMM’s epilogue. Each CTA publishes its completed tile directly from registers to peer GPUs through NVLink multicast stores while other tiles are still being computed. The consumer starts through PDL and waits for the published results before reducing them. This starts communication earlier and avoids rereading the partial output just to send it. The consumer’s computation remains unchanged.

blocks.text: The plugin moves the cross-GPU send into the GEMM epilogue. Both paths use two kernels; box sizes do not represent durations.

blocks.text: 3. Start the expert GEMMs before routing finishes. At low concurrency, routing can take a substantial share of the MoE path. With at most eight rows, each expert’s selected tokens fit in one eight-row tile. The plugin uses a bitmap and population counts to place these tiles without scanning or sorting while preserving SGLang’s top-k selections. It launches the first expert GEMM early to overlap setup with routing and skips an all-zero tile in the padded weights. The standard kernels already use eight-row tiles; the gains come from simpler routing, earlier execution and less wasted work. In the profiled runs, the median MoE window falls from 44.4 µs to 36.5 µs with little change in the second GEMM or reduction.

The plugin combines all five proposals into one kernel launch per GPU and keeps head weights in registers while coordinating token selection across GPUs. This reduces the profiled proposal span from 85.1 µs to 34.2 µs without changing SGLang’s speculative worker or acceptance logic.

blocks.text: At low concurrency, each decoder layer runs dozens of small kernels and two tensor-parallel all-reduces. Three costs dominate:

inlines.text: At low concurrency, each decoder layer runs dozens of small kernels and two tensor-parallel all-reduces. Three costs dominate:
Launch overhead:
HIP graphs remove the CPU's launch work, but each small kernel still costs 2-4 µs on the GPU.
Idle boundaries:
Each kernel must finish before the next starts, so compute units idle while one kernel drains and the next ramps up, and weight loading pauses.
Communication stops:
Each layer waits twice for an all-reduce across GPUs, with no computation running.

blocks.text: The plugin replaces dozens of small kernels with two persistent launches, loads weights early and overlaps the cross-GPU sums with computation. Box sizes do not represent durations.

inlines.text: The plugin replaces dozens of small kernels with two persistent launches, loads weights early and overlaps the cross-GPU sums with computation. Box sizes do not represent durations.

blocks.text: Two persistent launches per layer

inlines.text: Two persistent launches per layer

blocks.text: Persistent FlyDSL kernels combine most of each layer into two launches. K1 handles the mHC update, query and KV projections and KV-cache writes. K2 handles attention, output projections, the remaining mHC update, MoE and both all-reduces. Index layers add compression, K2i scoring and top-k between them. The launch boundary makes K1’s KV writes visible across the GPU before K2 reads them.

blocks.text: Each value a stage produces is stored together with a tag for the current decode step, so the next stage, on the same GPU or another one, starts on a value as soon as its tag matches. No separate flag or reset between steps is needed. Weights that do not depend on routing load before their inputs arrive: K1's projection weights before the norm finishes, and in K2 the mHC mix weights and the shared expert's weights before the data they multiply. Routed-expert weights load once the router has chosen the experts.

The MoE output is reduced the same way. Every cross-GPU wait has a deadline below SGLang's watchdog timeout; a missed deadline stops the launch on every GPU instead of hanging the server.

inlines.text: Plugin System: Design and Integration

blocks.text: Specialized kernels can require substantial amounts of code. Each combination of hardware, model architecture and parallel configuration may need its own implementation. Different workloads add further specialization. More combinations mean more code to review, test and maintain. Bringing every implementation into SGLang would make the core codebase increasingly difficult to maintain and place a growing workload on its reviewers and maintainers.

blocks.text: External kernel libraries connect to SGLang through registration, validation, build and runtime dispatch. The diagram shows the shared design; the AMD and NVIDIA interfaces are still evolving.

inlines.text: External kernel libraries connect to SGLang through registration, validation, build and runtime dispatch. The diagram shows the shared design; the AMD and NVIDIA interfaces are still evolving.

blocks.text: The plugin system connects these external libraries to SGLang through model specifications that declare their requirements and supported configurations. Kernel teams can develop their implementations independently while reusing SGLang’s scheduling and runtime resources.

inlines.text: The plugin system connects these external libraries to SGLang through model specifications that declare their requirements and supported configurations. Kernel teams can develop their implementations independently while reusing SGLang’s scheduling and runtime resources.

blocks.text: The integration separates startup preparation from execution:

inlines.text: The integration separates startup preparation from execution:
Register:

A plugin registers a specification for each model architecture it supports. The specification describes the implementation's requirements and provides the entry point for building it. This gives SGLang a way to discover external implementations while keeping the details of model support in the library that owns the kernels.
Guard:

Specialized kernels make assumptions about hardware, precision, parallelism and serving features. SGLang checks the declared requirements before loading weights so an incompatible configuration fails early. Additional checks on the loaded model run before the plugin is built. These checks distinguish an unsupported server configuration from a supported server encountering a step outside the plugin's coverage.
Build:

Weight preparation and execution resources are set up during initialization so requests can reuse them. The integration accommodates the needs of each implementation: AMD can retain checkpoint tensors before weight conversion, while NVIDIA receives a binding through which it can access runtime state as that state becomes available. SGLang builds the plugin before sizing the KV cache so its allocations are accounted for, then installs dispatch in the model's forward path.
Runtime:

Specialized and general execution coexist because a plugin may cover only certain step types and token counts. The installed dispatcher uses the plugin's support conditions to select its forward or SGLang's original forward. Tensor-parallel ranks must agree on coverage to avoid entering incompatible collectives. This selection fits into ModelRunner's existing execution flow. During graph capture, the chosen path is recorded for that shape; serving can then replay the graph without repeating Python dispatch.

blocks.text: This design lets kernel teams ship focused optimizations without adding every specialized implementation to SGLang's core codebase. It concentrates integration work at explicit interfaces and allows each library to expand its coverage incrementally. Specialized kernels can serve the cases they optimize while SGLang's general forward handles the remaining steps within a supported configuration.

inlines.text: CI and Performance Validation

blocks.text: External kernel implementations sit outside SGLang's regular code review process. Strong CI coverage at the plugin interface is therefore essential to verify that these implementations meet SGLang's correctness and runtime requirements. We plan to test compatibility checks, weight binding, forward outputs and state updates, including KV-cache writes. End-to-end tests will also cover graph execution, fallback behavior and performance regressions as SGLang and the external libraries evolve.

blocks.text: Evolving Shared Plugin Interfaces

inlines.text: Evolving Shared Plugin Interfaces

blocks.text: Although the plugin framework is now in place, it is still at an early stage. We expect to refine its interfaces and design through long-term iteration as we integrate more kernels and learn from their use in production.
